entries.text: Arduino sketch: setup() runs once (pinMode, Serial.begin(115200)), loop() runs forever; avoid delay() in anything with more than one task - use millis() timing instead.
Arduino I/O: digitalWrite/digitalRead for pins, analogRead (0-1023) for sensors, analogWrite (0-255 PWM) for brightness/speed; use INPUT_PULLUP for buttons and debounce them.
Embedded memory is tiny: prefer fixed-size buffers and uint8_t/uint16_t, avoid String objects and dynamic allocation on 8-bit boards, store constant text with F("...") / PROGMEM.

C: every malloc needs a free, every array index needs a bounds check, every string needs a terminator; compile with `gcc -Wall -Wextra -g file.c -o prog` and run under valgrind or ASan for memory errors.
C++: prefer std::vector/std::string/std::array over raw arrays, RAII and smart pointers (unique_ptr) over new/delete, and `auto` + range-for loops; build with `g++ -std=c++20 -Wall`.
Serial debugging on microcontrollers: print state changes, not every loop iteration; match the baud rate in the monitor; a device that resets repeatedly usually has a power or stack overflow problem.
